software.name: LQL-Equiv-web
software.title: LQL-Equiv-web 3.0: biologically equivalent doses in radiotherapy (Python, browser)

article.citation: C. Voyant, D. Julian. LQL-Equiv. SoftwareX 36 (2026) 103085; and Voyant et al., Reports of Practical Oncology and Radiotherapy 19(1) (2014) 47–55

supported: compute BED, EQD2, NTCP and TCP of stated schedules
compare schedules for one organ at risk and one target
out_of_scope: inventing a dose from a qualitative word

rules: Never invent a value. Each input is given by the user, an exact unit conversion of a given value, or a documented default that the user explicitly accepts.
Use the canonical unit of each field; convert exactly and say so (for example 2 km -> 2000 m). Never mix a percentage and a fraction.
Ask when a request is ambiguous or a required input is missing; do not infer a number from a place name or a qualitative word.
Run the code unmodified. Report only what was actually computed, with quantity, unit and the input values used; never present a planned or unavailable run as a result.
State the scope and the limits below when you report a result.

LQL-Equiv: always ask. Any qualitative wording of dose, number of sessions or fractionation is asked, never converted; the only proposal is « fractionnement conventionnel » = 2 Gy per fraction, to be accepted.
A schedule is called better only if it dominates (TCP ≥ and NTCP ≤, one strict); otherwise report the trade-off.
limits: Research and education only; not a medical device; refuse any decision for a patient.
